title: Local trace consumer oddities - scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes while debugging weird behavior in the local trace consumer (running on my laptop + kube dev cluster). Trying to capture commands tried, observations, and hypotheses so I can hand off or revisit later.

TL;DR:
- trace-consumer-v2 intermittently shows 0 processed messages in app metrics while Kafka offsets advance and traces disappear from downstream storage (BigQuery).
- Symptoms coincide with short spikes of broker CPU/network, and with logagent restarts in the same node pool.
- Repro steps below + candidate hypotheses (consumer commit timing, partial decode, backpressure -> early ack).

Immediate reproducer (dev cluster):
1) kubectl port-forward svc/kafka 9092:9092 -n infra
2) docker run --rm -it --network host confluentinc/cp-kafka:latest bash
3) kafka-console-producer --broker-list localhost:9092 --topic traces.raw <-- push sample event (see sample_event.json below)
4) watch pod logs: kubectl logs -f deploy/trace-consumer-v2 -n observability
5) watch metrics endpoint: curl -s localhost:9102/metrics | grep trace_consumer_processed_total

Observed outputs/commands I've run:
- kubectl get pods -n observability --watch -> saw consumer pod get Restarted 1/3 during incident window (node preempted).
- kubectl logs deploy/trace-consumer-v2 -c consumer-main -n observability | grep -i error
  -> repeated: "ERROR decode_span: unexpected EOF while reading length-prefix" (see snippets below)
- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --describe --group trace-consumer-group
  -> offsets increasing, lag ~0, consumer state stable (no rebalances) but app metric shows processed_total = 0 for some intervals
- curl -s http://localhost:9102/metrics | grep trace_consumer_processed_total
  -> 0
- curl -s http://localhost:9102/metrics | grep trace_consumer_commit_latency_seconds_bucket
  -> buckets show a spike at ~0.1s then nothing for 60s windows

Sample error lines copied from logs:
- 2026-02-25T14:03:02Z ERROR decode_span id=8f4a12b4 msg="unexpected EOF while reading length-prefix" consumer_offset=10432
- 2026-02-25T14:03:02Z WARN  span_dropped id=8f4a12b4 reason=decode_error
- 2026-02-25T14:03:03Z INFO  commit offset=10433 partition=12 latency_ms=7
- 2026-02-25T14:03:10Z INFO  metrics_flush interval=60s processed=0

Sample event (small, intentionally truncated to exercise decode error):
{
  "trace_id": "8f4a12b4...",
  "spans": [ { "id": "1", "name": "http.server", "attributes": {"http.status_code": 200 } } ]
}
(we sometimes receive length-prefixed protobufs; truncation can happen if logagent tailer flushes partial frames)

Initial notes and mental model:
- Consumer reads amplify messages (protobuf length-prefix). If consumer sees EOF mid-frame it logs decode_error and drops span. But that alone shouldn't set processed_total to 0 if other messages processed.
- Kafka offsets advancing + processed_total=0 means either: 1) consumer increments commit before processing, or 2) processed_total counter is reset (metrics exporter restart), or 3) processed messages are filtered/dropped downstream before metrics increment.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Early commit due to error path: code does commit in finally{} even on decode errors, and metrics increment lives after processing pipeline. If decode error occurs before processed counter increment, offset is committed but metric doesn't increment -> looks like "lost" traces.
   - Repro: inject truncated frames -> offsets move, processed counter stays flat.
   - Fix direction: move commit to after successful processing or add a per-message dead-letter queue.

2) Metrics exporter register/flush bug: when the consumer process gets SIGHUP (logagent or sidecar causing container restarts), the Prometheus client registry is reinitialized and previous counters reset to zero until process accumulates again. If restarts are frequent, metrics appear as zeros for windows.
   - Evidence: pod restarts seen in k8s events around incident periods.
   - Mitigation: ensure metrics registry is global and not re-created on hot-reload; persist last-known counters? (ugly)

3) Partial decode + batch ack: consumer batches messages (N=128) and commits offset for whole batch once processed. If first message in batch raises decode_error and code currently commits batch anyway (to avoid reprocessing poisons), downstream sees gaps.
   - Check batch commit code path: source file consumer/worker.go line ~412 (local copy).

4) Logagent/inflight chop: the log agent that tails files (logagent v1.14) emits partial protobuf frames when rotate occurs. Those partial frames enter Kafka and look like short messages -> decode_error path. Should ideally be filtered upstream.
   - Evidence: timestamps of rotating logs in node correlate with last 3 incidents.

Quick code snippets I grepped through locally:
- grep -nR "decode_span" -n src/consumer | head
- cat src/consumer/worker.go | sed -n '380,460p'
  -> finally { commitOffsets(); cleanup() }   // suspect commit always runs

Prometheus / metrics investigation notes:
- Prom client version: 0.11.0 (Go) used in consumer image tag: redwood/trace-consumer:v2.1.7
- Metric definitions: trace_consumer_processed_total (counter), exported via push-gateway? no, pull via /metrics endpoint
- If process restarts quickly, scrape sees start at 0. But Kafka offsets show continuity.

Kafka checks performed:
- kafka-topics --describe --topic traces.raw -> partitions 24, retention 7d
- kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group trace-consumer-group -> shows offsets increasing, consumer id trace-consumer-v2-abc active, lags near 0
- kafka-run-class kafka.tools.SimpleConsumerShell -> pulled a few raw messages; some messages are clearly truncated (length smaller than length-prefix)

Correlation timeline (abridged):
- 2026-02-25T13:58Z -> node pool autoscaler kicked, some nodes cordoned
- 2026-02-25T14:01Z -> kubelet restarted logagent pod on node-14
- 2026-02-25T14:03Z -> consumer pod restarted once
- 2026-02-25T14:04Z -> BigQuery sink job reports missing rows for trace buckets [2026-02-25 14:00 - 14:05]

Immediate next steps (local):
- Add additional logging around commitOffsets() in local dev build (print offsets + commitReason).
- Run consumer in "dry-run" mode: do not commit offsets, just print what would be committed for 60s.
  Commands: docker build -t riley/trace-consumer:debug . && docker run --env DRY_RUN=1 ...
- Introduce temporary filter in logagent to drop messages < 64 bytes or with malformed length-prefix and observe effect.
- Add a per-message success counter earlier in pipeline (increment as soon as message decoded) to isolate whether decode vs commit ordering is the problem.

Longer-term mitigations to propose in Jira:
- Implement a dead-letter topic for decode errors and stop committing those offsets automatically.
- Harden logagent tailer to assemble length-prefixed frames across rotations.
- Review commit logic to ensure commits happen after ack of message processing, not in finally/unconditional path.
- Add a "processed_by_component" tag to metrics so we can distinguish consumer-level processing vs downstream sink acceptance.

Notes-to-self (things I tried that were worthless):
- bumping consumer concurrency from 8->16 didn't change symptom (offsets same, processed_total still zero in windows)
- changing Kafka retention or partition count irrelevant for short window testing

Useful grep / inspect commands to rerun later:
- kubectl logs -n observability deploy/trace-consumer-v2 --since=2h | grep "decode_span" | wc -l
- kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --topic traces.raw --from-beginning --max-messages 500 | jq -r '. | length' | sort -n | uniq -c
- kubectl get events -n observability --field-selector reason=Killing -o wide --watch

Hand-off checklist if I need to escalate to oncall:
- attach these notes + timestamps + pod names + sample truncated messages in JIRA-OBS-4382
- run the dry-run build and share logs with SRE
- set temporary alert: if trace_consumer_processed_total == 0 and kafka offsets advanced > 100 in 5m -> pager to eng-observability oncall

Random trace-id I kept for when I need to search other systems: 8f4a12b4a7c9e152 (use as anchor for logs across ingest, consumer, bq sink)

-- end of scratchpad --
